$comment: THE LIST CI RUNS, not a description of one (#396, stage 1).
scripts/run-checks.mjs iterates this file and ci.yml invokes that runner, so an entry
here IS an execution. A declared list CI did not iterate would be a second source of
truth and worse than the YAML it replaced: it would report a set nobody ran.
Each entry runs its PROOF first and its CHECKER second, in one process, because a
checker whose proof did not run is a checker nobody has watched fail. That ordering was
previously spelled out in six separate `pnpm <name>` scripts chaining `&&`; it is now a
property of the runner, so it cannot be forgotten on the seventh.
STAGE 1 covers only the six that already had the proof-first form. The other 45 checker
steps in ci.yml keep their own steps and pairing keeps parsing YAML for them.

checks.name: route-stubs
checks.why: a route stub matching more than one real endpoint answers requests it was never written for (#379)

checks.name: fixture-premises
checks.why: a fixture that plants into a directory-owned glob must say so, or a reparent leaves it green about nothing (#375)

checks.name: manifest-coupling
checks.why: rung coupling that travels through the generated types (#374)

checks.name: langfuse-wiring
checks.why: observability wiring present in every backend, not only the one someone tested

checks.name: github-reporter
checks.why: a failing e2e job names the test that failed (#362)

checks.name: run-axes-parity
checks.why: the run axes agree across backends rather than each backend deciding separately

checks.name: required-contexts
checks.why: branch protection names required checks in a second place, and a rename makes the two disagree in silence in one direction and in permanent deadlock in the other (#404)
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, NOT A SNAPSHOT. The derivation run reported 32 and a floor of 32 was a SCHEDULED FAILURE: this subject is the branch-protection required-context list, which is external config, so retiring one CI job drops it to 31 and the check refuses — reporting 'a green whose subject is under the floor' about a tree that is fine. What the floor needs to catch is an EMPTY result (the API answered with nothing), and 1 does that completely. Found by DEV3-lang.

checks.name: undeclared-reverts
checks.why: a branch can undo merged work with every pre-merge gate green, because a revert is self-consistent — its tests are reverted with its code (#406)
checks.floorNote: NO FLOOR EXISTS, EVER — same class as `formatted`. It compares CHANGED files, so its 31 was one branch's diff size; clean main reports 21. Measured on both trees, not inferred from reading it.

checks.name: coverage-surface
checks.why: a shared surface covered only by rung-owned specs loses its tests to an eject while keeping the feature (#373)

checks.name: overrides-inert
checks.why: an override carrying a version selector stops applying once a resolution rises above it, and reads as protection while doing nothing (#378)

checks.name: ladder-is-cumulative
checks.why: #788. assert-every-rung-is-witnessed:9 says the ladder being cumulative is "a real guarantee stated nowhere". It has two dependents that would both stay green if it stopped holding: rung-witnessing (a rung nothing removes is never shown severable) and #755's audit (eject-to-rung-1 treated as the maximal strip, so a subject static under it is static under every weaker target). This asserts the CONSEQUENCE both rely on — closure(requires, N) == the rungs at or below ordinal N — rather than the chain shape that currently produces it
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR. Its subject is the rung count, legitimately 1 in a rung-1 fork and 5 on main — and forks are exactly where severability is measured, so a floor at the observed 5 would refuse where this matters most. A floor of 1 catches the vacuity that matters: a manifest with no rungs.

checks.name: census-survives-the-merge
checks.why: #145's silent half: two branches each adding one rung-owned file both freeze N+1 from a base of N, so git sees the same number on both sides, merges cleanly, and the merged tree holds N+2 declaring N+1. assert-census-fresh already catches exactly this and its SILENT case proves it — but it was invoked once, gated to pull_request, asking about a BRANCH merging into its base. Nobody asked it about two branches merging into each other, which is what a batch is. Measured: on such a merged tree classify.mjs, census.mjs and freeze-all.mjs all exit 0, so wiring those in closes nothing
checks.floorNote: NOT DERIVED YET, and a floor probably EXISTS. This check refuses on a non-merge HEAD, so the derivation run could not reach it. Derive it from a run on a MERGE COMMIT and replace this note. `floorPending` marks it so a later run can be told which entries to derive, and so a reader can tell this apart from a floor that can never exist.

checks.name: merge-keeps-registrations
checks.why: two branches appending to one registration list conflict, and taking either side wholesale drops the other's entry — for this very file that means a checker that never runs (#467)
checks.floorNote: NOT DERIVED YET, same gate: it refuses on a non-merge HEAD. A positive floor would be a guess about a run nobody has taken. Derive from a merge commit and replace this note.

checks.name: barrel-type-exports
checks.why: a type-only export dropped from the barrel is invisible to the runtime completeness guard and still compiles, so tsc is silent and the break surfaces at a consumer (#446)

checks.name: parity-tsconfig
checks.why: a cross-package suite excluded from the package program and absent from the parity include is in NO program: green, and never typechecked (#430)

checks.name: testmatch-anchored
checks.why: an unanchored testMatch means 'this spec' to a reader and 'any path containing this substring' to the engine, so a suffix-named file joins a project silently and runs against the wrong app (#475)

checks.name: e2e-partition
checks.why: a spec gaining or losing a project changes what it is tested against and reports the same green; emptiness checks cannot see it because the spec still runs somewhere and the project still runs something (#475)

checks.name: swallowed-evidence
checks.why: vitest's default reporter swallows console output from a PASSING test, so a check that names its subject with console.log prints nothing and looks exactly like one that never named it (#456)

checks.name: behavioural-evidence
checks.why: a behavioural requirement closed by an existence check reads as satisfied while the behaviour is absent — ADAPT-05 said the run pauses and was satisfied by three exports and a test count (#453)

checks.name: board-declarations
checks.why: the v2.0 label and the v2.0 milestone are two declarations of one fact; when they drift the milestone-filtered board reads as shippable while the label view does not, and the drift has recurred three times (#410)
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR, same reason. Its subject is the OPEN ISSUE COUNT read over the network, and the vacuity its own header documents is '403 / rate limit / rotated token -> 0 issues -> 0 disagreements -> PASS'. A floor of 1 catches that entirely. The derived 9 was two closures from failing, on a board that closed eighteen issues in a day.

checks.name: verdict-tokens-disjoint
checks.why: a selftest fixture's verdict printed in the real format, on the same stream in the same job, reads as a real transport defect — and a fixture PASS would read as a clean transport (#496)

checks.name: rung-witnesses
checks.why: a rung no severability cell removes has never been shown severable, and every cell stays green because each one only speaks about its own removals (#495)

checks.name: playwright-history
checks.why: captureGitInfo.diff defaults ON under CI and depth-fetches the PR base into the workspace, so every later history read sees one commit and every file as added there — silently, in whatever tool runs next (#470)

checks.name: graph-id-agreement
checks.why: rung 4's multi-graph fixture copies rung 5's graph ids as literals -- correctly, since reading that file would break an ejected fork -- so nothing stops an upstream rename leaving the fixture green about a backend that no longer exists (#454)

checks.name: graph-list-doc-claim
checks.why: the docs a person reads to decide what upstream registers restate its graph list in prose; deriving it is not available -- the repo already generates one such sentence from a hand-maintained template, which moved the copy rather than removing it (#468)

checks.name: workflow-event-matrix
checks.why: a fork inherits the workflows, so E2E-05's claim about which jobs run on which events -- and skip on fork PRs -- is a claim about what a forker gets; the absence half is satisfied by a workflow where those jobs run for nobody, so presence is asserted with it (E2E-05, CI-01)

checks.name: readme-vocabulary
checks.why: the README's vocabulary table is a second declaration of the manifest's field set, and prose does not run (#487)

checks.name: fork-python-imports
checks.why: a SHARED python test importing a RUNG-OWNED module collects fine in the full tree and dies with an ImportError in every fork below that rung; ruff --select F821 and the boot check are both structurally blind to it (#565)

checks.name: formatted
checks.why: this repo has checkers and tests that parse source TEXT, so whitespace is an input to a verdict rather than a matter of taste — a re-indent already made a parity reader find nothing (#463). Scoped to the files a branch changed: the 651-file backlog (at 8c9172bf) is cleared separately under #406's detector, because a repo-wide reformat is the one diff nobody reads line by line (#405)
checks.floorNote: NO FLOOR EXISTS, EVER. Its subject is the CHANGED-FILE set, not the tree: the derivation run reported 38 because that was one branch's diff, and on clean main the same checker reports 52. A branch touching one file honestly examines 1, and a merge touching none examines 0. This is not pending — a diff-subject cannot carry a floor. Non-vacuity for this class needs a RELATIVE invariant (subject == the changed files it was given), which is deliberately not in this change.

checks.name: ismain-guards-resolve
checks.why: a script deciding isMain by comparing a resolved path to an unresolved one runs nothing through a symlink and exits 0, which reads as a pass (#631)

checks.name: scan-exclusions-justified
checks.why: an unexplained --exclude in the security scan is a hole nobody can notice has stopped being justified, and the job is green whether it looks or not (#632)

checks.name: dev-planes-startable
checks.why: a runtime rungs.json declares that pnpm dev cannot start is a plane nobody can bring up, and dev-all.sh is run by people so no gate would ever notice (#633)

checks.name: example-approval-policy
checks.why: the reference app sends the Python backends a read-only allowlist, which is a second statement of _common.py's @tool set with nothing asserting they agree; a new tool ships gated-by-default and unclassified, a removed one lingers, and both drifts are silent (#653)

checks.name: the checkpointer comes from the shared seam
checks.why: #643 replaced one module-level InMemorySaver with six call sites, three rungs across two planes. A rung that quietly builds its own saver keeps passing every approval test and simply ignores an injected one, so the drift is silent in the direction that matters. This also holds the scope: derive_thread_id puts no rung in the thread id, so two rungs resolving the same scope share a thread for the same session — measured at 2 leaked messages with one saver, 0 with separate ones.

checks.name: both planes drive the same decision vocabulary
checks.why: #668's ruling made enforceable. check-run-axes-parity is SOURCE-ONLY and covers the files it compares; the approval decision path runs through main.py/views.py, which it reads for a property and never for identity — 379 lines against 213, where identity is impossible. So a decision asserted on one plane says nothing about the other, which is how the whole vocabulary sat on fastapi alone until #671. This reads the literals passed to each plane's approvalDecisions helper rather than searching for decision names, because a suite that names all four in a docstring and sends three is what a grep passes.

checks.name: build-order
checks.why: a package built before its dependency reads a stale dist, and the failure blames the newest edit rather than the ordering (#590)

checks.name: child-process-argv-form
checks.why: a child process spawned with a shell string re-parses its own arguments, so a path with a space becomes two paths and the call still exits 0

checks.name: cross-browser-coverage
checks.why: a restriction pinned per ENGINE rather than per test, so removing one browser's only case shows as a number moving rather than as silence (#749)

checks.name: error-frame-contract
checks.why: a rename on the emitting side alone ends all attribution, and the classifier answers FAILED_UNCLASSIFIED for every origin without anything going red

checks.name: index-paths-exist
checks.why: the script index naming a file the tree does not have, and a Pending section that never terminates exempting every list below it (#762)

checks.name: no-missing-workspace-invocations
checks.why: a --filter naming a workspace that does not exist runs nothing and exits 0, which reads exactly like a package with no work to do

checks.name: no-silent-skips
checks.why: a test skipped unconditionally with no declared reason is a case nobody can tell has stopped meaning anything

checks.name: no-verdict-destroying-pipelines
checks.why: a verdict piped into grep or head takes the LAST stage's exit status, so a failing command reports the success of its filter (#736)

checks.name: readme-quickstart
checks.why: a Quick Start naming symbols a package does not export sends a forker to an API that is not there

checks.name: rung5-security-patches
checks.why: the #82 and #84 behaviours are what rung 5 is FOR, and a fork that drops them keeps the name without the property

checks.name: sibling-tests-are-owned
checks.why: a sibling test owned by a different rung than its subject is collected in the full tree and dies at import in every fork below that rung (#716)

checks.name: single-instance
checks.why: two copies of one module in a bundle give two module-level registries, and the second silently answers for state the first holds (RCT-04)

checks.name: checkers-registered
checks.why: eighteen checkers sat unregistered and the sixteenth arrived the same way the fifteenth did — that is the absence of a gate, not carelessness, and without this the registrations are a one-time tidy with a known repair (#741)

checks.name: eject-subjects-classified
checks.why: a subject count can be PRINTED rather than computed, and #741's floor cannot see it (#755). This gate is the cheap half: it asserts every registered checker has an eject classification. The measurement that produces them is `pnpm eject-audit`, ~5 minutes, on demand.
checks.floorNote: VACUITY FLOOR. Its subject is the registered-checker count, which is >= 1 by construction whenever checks.json is non-empty; the floor exists to catch a reading that enumerated nothing, not to bound the registry's size. THE OBSERVED SHA IS A PRE-SQUASH BRANCH COMMIT, DELIBERATELY. A brand-new check cannot cite a sha on main — this checker does not exist at b22774ec, so counting 48 there is impossible, and inventing a main sha to look durable would name a tree where the measurement could not have been taken. 325006a7 is this branch merged with main, which is a tree someone can check out and re-measure; it does not survive the squash, and that is the honest cost of a first anchor. Same trade as the census's `measuredAt` vs `base` (#755). AND THE RECORD IS DECORATIVE FOR THIS ENTRY (#811). `floorObserved` exists so a DERIVED number can be confirmed or falsified against the tree it came from. This floor is 1 — a vacuity floor, chosen rather than derived — so the sha confirms nothing about it. Having a `floorObserved` is not the same as having provenance, and this one is present because the gate requires it rather than because it carries information.

unregistered.reason: it runs, but not from here — and it cannot. WHERE IT RUNS: .github/workflows/ci.yml, job `python:`, step "The approval vocabulary we offer is one the parser accepts (#669)" — which invokes `node scripts/assert-approval-vocabulary-agrees.selftest.mjs` and then the checker with `--python "$(command -v python)"`, after that job's `pip install -r requirements.txt` under `working-directory: apps/fastapi-backend`. That working directory is load-bearing: there is no requirements.txt at the repo root. Anchored on the job and step NAMES rather than line numbers, because rewriting the step's own comment in #771 moved the invocation by eight lines and stale line numbers in this field would be the same defect this entry documents. WHY IT CANNOT BE REGISTERED HERE: it asks an INSTALLED langchain what `interrupt_on={tool: True}` expands to, so it only runs where the backend requirements are installed, and `pnpm checks` runs in job `ci:`, which never installs them — registering it here would exit 2 on every run. NOT A CHANNEL, DELIBERATELY: a channel would convert that loud exit 2 into a quiet, correct, permanent NOT MEASURED, and run-checks.mjs makes exactly that argument about itself for `repo-settings` — a channel needs somewhere it is satisfied, and this one would have none. Exiting 2 when the interpreter cannot answer is the behaviour to keep. Permanent while `pnpm checks` runs in a job without the backend requirements; installing them there is the only thing that would change it, and it has not been judged worth a pip install on every node run.
requires run-specific arguments — it needs a base and a head, and the runner passes none.
consumes the runner's own output — it reads .checks-run.json, which run-checks WRITES. A check registered here would read a record of a run that had not finished.

not a node script — run-checks spawns `process.execPath <script>` (run-checks.mjs:484), so this would run as `node x.sh`. AND it requires run-specific arguments (`--label`, `--forbid-module`, positional subjects; ci.yml:838), so a port to .mjs would not admit it either. Two independent reasons.

its subject is an install that has not happened yet. It runs at ci.yml:89, BEFORE `pnpm install` at :92, deliberately; `pnpm checks` is at :790. A registered copy would run where the install has necessarily already succeeded, so it could never fail — a vacuous entry. The argument is ci.yml:82's, which predates this change.

requires run-specific arguments — `--record <file>` or `--verify <file> --retained a,b,c`. Found by RUNNING it, not by reading: clause 2 has no fixed vocabulary, and a scan for --base/--head/--at does not see --record/--verify.

not a checker — it is `pnpm format`, the developer command that REWRITES the tree. A checker that writes would be a control running downstream of its own effect. CI runs `pnpm test:format` (its proof, by mutation) but never `pnpm format`, and that asymmetry is deliberate: the gate that asserts formatting is `formatted` in this file, which reads and does not write. Its proof running is not it running.

not a checker — it is `pnpm freeze:all`, the maintainer command that SETTLES the frozen artifacts other checkers compare against. It writes the baseline; asserting against a baseline you just wrote is the shape a control must not have. Its proof runs in CI; the command is run by hand before committing a moved number.

not a checker — it MEASURES and does not assert, and its own header opens by saying so. It has no failing verdict to give: it partitions flake occurrences for a human to read, and is imported by verdict-streak.mjs. Registering it would demand a floor and a subject for a number that is an observation rather than a claim.

not a checker — its header states the rule directly: "Property measured, not asserted". It reports how long a red survives on a push-only job. Imported by verdict-streak.mjs. NOTE, and this is the only one of the six where it is true: its own proof is invoked by no workflow either, so nothing exercises it in CI at all. That is worth its own issue rather than a silent line here.

not a checker — it is the shared harness that mutation-based PROOFS import, so it executes whenever they do, as a module rather than as a program. Nothing invokes it as a step and nothing should. It is in this population only because it has a proof of its own, which is correct: a harness that silently stopped mutating would make every proof that uses it vacuous.

not a checker — a helper imported by census.mjs and classify.mjs to write a generated JSON artifact in the shape the format gate expects. Executed as a module by its importers, never invoked as a step.

NOT A CHECKER — a measurement tool, and registering it would put a five-minute run on every PR. WHERE IT RUNS: `pnpm eject-audit` (package.json), on demand, by whoever adds or changes a checker — because scripts/assert-eject-subjects-classified.mjs is the registered gate that tells them to. WHY IT CANNOT BE REGISTERED: measured, not estimated — it runs the full check suite TWICE, 193s on the full tree and 191s on an ejected one, plus a 2s eject, a 5s install and a ~25s build of each. That is the 'minutes' branch of #755's split: the gate is cheap and total and runs per PR; this produces the entries the gate checks for. Registering it would buy one measurement of a small changing subset at the cost of measuring all 48 on every PR. NOT A CHANNEL, DELIBERATELY: a channel would turn a loud 'the census is stale' into a quiet permanent NOT MEASURED, and a channel needs somewhere it is satisfied — this one would have none, because there is no CI job that should spend ten minutes on it. Permanent while the audit costs minutes; if the check suite ever became seconds this could be registered like anything else, and that is the only thing that would change it.

NOT A CHECKER — the PRODUCER for scripts/eject-subject-audit.mjs, and unregistered for the same measured reason that one is: it runs the full check suite TWICE and additionally ejects, installs and builds a second worktree, so ~7-8 minutes on every PR to measure a subset that changes only when someone registers a checker. WHERE IT RUNS: `pnpm eject-audit`, on demand, by whoever the registered gate scripts/assert-eject-subjects-classified.mjs has just told to run it. WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL (#819): that gate's remediation named `pnpm eject-audit`, and `pnpm eject-audit` was wired straight to the CONSUMER, which refuses without four arguments no workflow supplied and no example anywhere in the tree demonstrated. The instruction could not be followed, and the first person to hit it correctly stopped rather than guess — guessing would have produced the plausible-but-wrong census the audit's own header warns about. ITS PROOF IS CHEAP AND IS NOT THIS: scripts/eject-audit-run.selftest.mjs covers every decision made before anything expensive runs, plus the record check made after, which is the set that decides whether a bad census can be written. Permanent while the audit costs minutes — the same condition that governs the consumer, and the only thing that would change it.
